doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing with Chick Corea on The Ultimate Adventure
summary: Laws says playing with Chick Corea is always a challenge and that he learns from Chick's spontaneous creativity.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Nancy Wilson, Turned to Blue. Now we’re into 2005, 2006. So we’re getting pretty close. Valerie King. Then Chick Corea, The Ultimate Adventure.

Yes, man. Whoo. Chick Corea. That guy is so creative. I tell you. That was another challenge. It’s always a challenge, playing with Chick, but I’m getting better. I’m getting better, because it made me practice more improvisation, because I see how that guy is so creative. I sit there night after night and watch him just play stuff. There’s stuff just oozing out of him. There’s just different stuff, like compo- – really compositions, spontaneously. I learn from that. I learn even how to practice better.
